boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Charleston Harbor II record (September 7-8, 1863) in Operations Against the Defenses of Charleston [April-September 1863]. The evacuation of Wagner and Gregg on the night of September 6-7 closes SC007; the Moultrie engagement of September 7-8 and the boat attack on Sumter of the night of September 8-9 are both reported in the inspected passages. Campaign-wide marches, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen force text reads Regiments: total unknown (US 413; CS unknown), with a frozen US bound of 413; the live page gives 413 (US 413; CS 0) and describes a storming party of about 400 marines and sailors. Jones says the naval storming party was 450 picked sailors and marines, of whom eleven officers and 116 men landed, that Gillmore's own party was six or seven hundred infantry, and that the Sumter garrison was the First South Carolina Battalion, 205 men, one third kept under arms. For the Moultrie action he names the New Ironsides and five monitors.
claims.rationale: Party and garrison figures from a history; the basis of the frozen 413 is not stated in any inspected passage. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. Gillmore says the naval assault was repulsed with considerable loss and his own was abandoned; Jones says the attack failed completely in about twenty minutes. Gillmore also records the Union occupation of the north end of Morris Island on the 7th.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads (US 117; CS unknown); the live field reads 217 (US 117; CS 100). Jones says of the landed party 6 were killed, 15 wounded and 106 captured, with five barges and five colors; at Moultrie on the 8th an explosion killed sixteen and wounded twelve, and three more were killed and two officers and fourteen men wounded.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Jones's landed-party figures (6 killed, 15 wounded and 106 captured) and the frozen 117 differ; the Moultrie losses belong to the ironclad engagement, not the boat attack.

open_questions: Dahlgren's and Stephens's naval reports (Official Records of the Navies I, 14), Elliott's report, the Moultrie reports and the Union boat-party casualty returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (NPS battle page and frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Quincy A. Gillmore's report dated February 28, 1864 (Official Records I, XXVIII part 1, No. 2) is one family of interested Union accounts. Samuel Jones's The Siege of Charleston (1911) is a posthumous Confederate general's history that quotes Gillmore's, Seymour's, Strong's, Ripley's, Taliaferro's and Beauregard's reports and is not independent of them. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
